races.title: State House, District 26
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Donna McDowell White
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 26 (northern Johnston County) since 2017. Previously served on the Johnston County Board of Education, where she chaired the finance committee, per her 2016 campaign site. Has been House Appropriations vice chair and chaired Health and Appropriations on Health and Human Services.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she moved to North Carolina; the only biographical detail found is her birth date, November 29, 1948. We found no documented actions or stated positions of hers on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her 2016 campaign site mentions growth in Johnston County only as a topic for collaboration, not a position. Ballotpedia lists her sponsored bills and scorecards by name only, with no content we could read. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, and Ballotpedia found no endorsements for 2024 or 2026. Her full work history before the school board is not documented in the pages we had. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the sources.

qual.background: Nine years in the NC House (2017 to 2027), including Appropriations vice chair. Earlier she served on the Johnston County Board of Education and, by her own 2016 campaign account, chaired its finance committee during a $61 million funding loss. She describes nurse-related work.
qual.why: Prior legislative service of several terms plus local elected office with budget responsibility fits the writing-law-and-budget job. Committee chair posts were not counted. The score stops short of the top because her pre-legislative career details are thin and mostly self-reported.

cands.name: L'Bertrice Solomon
cands.bio: Dr. L'Bertrice Solomon is a Johnston County resident, minister and Chief Public Health Officer for Docs On Da Block. Her campaign materials also describe her as informed by public health and law. She was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 26 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Lillian's List, Planned Parenthood (PPVSAT) and Johnston County Down Home, per her Ballotpedia survey. She is also a 2026 Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate.
Voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups, including Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Imani's Pix, NC GIRLIES, Unburdening The Ballot and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Solomon was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no dates or details for her career, and no confirmation of a law degree or legal work. She has no prior elected office on record. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B visas, police pay, or gun laws beyond a Moms Demand Action designation. We found no documented actions in office and no controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Chief Public Health Officer for Docs On Da Block, a minister, and a public health professional whose work spans hospital wards and community health fairs. The campaign site says her leadership is 'informed by public health and law', but no legal career or prior elected office is documented.

pro-life.evidence: Said women deserve meaningful access to comprehensive healthcare and the ability to make personal healthcare decisions without unnecessary barriers to care.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said she wants thoughtful, responsible growth, with infrastructure keeping pace with development and residents having a voice in decisions. This is a general stance, not a specific land-use pledge.
